Q. 69. What is the communion in grace which the members of the invisible church have with Christ?

A. The communion in grace which the members of the invisible church have with Christ, is their partaking of the virtue of his mediation, in their justification, adoption, sanctification, and whatever else, in this life, manifests their union with him.

occurrences.excerpt: 4. Justification - That TE Leithart in his views and teachings fails, contrary to Scripture and the Westminster Standards, to properly distinguish justification from sanctification (WLC 69, 75, 77 and Rom 3:28; Rom 4:4-8; Rom 12:1; Titus 3:4-8).

metadata.synopsis: The SJC denied RE Gerald Hedman's complaint against Pacific Northwest Presbytery, which had adopted five not-guilty judgments on charges that TE Peter Leithart's baptism, covenant, imputation, justification, and union-with-Christ views contradicted the Westminster Standards. Bound to the record and clear-error review, the SJC found no procedural violation and insufficient evidence that Presbytery clearly erred. It left the verdicts undisturbed, declined to endorse Leithart's views generally, and urged continued clarification of his non-standard terminology. A separate dissent would have found error and ordered a new trial or reference.

metadata.synopsis: In a BCO 40-5 memorial, Central Carolina Presbytery alleged that Louisiana Presbytery had exonerated TE J. Steven Wilkins despite his published views on election, the church, perseverance, assurance, and baptism allegedly contradicting the Westminster Standards. The SJC sustained the memorial’s gravity and found Presbytery failed to show due diligence, ordering a recorded examination, formal responses, and report. Presbytery later met the procedural directives, but the SJC relied on Case 2007-8’s substantive finding, cited Presbytery under BCO 40-5, and appointed a prosecutor for Case 2007-14.
